title: regional-gpu-scaling-scenarios-2026-2027
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc captures three realistic scaling scenarios for Redwood's GPU fleet across North America (NA), Europe (EU), and APAC for 2026–H1 2027. It focuses on:
- per-region target GPU inventory (by class: H100, A100, A800 as applicable)
- expected utilization curves and triggers for procurement/provisioning
- phased rollout timelines and staging (staggered activation to avoid cold-start spikes)
- fallback and buffer strategies (burst pools, spot vs reserved mix)
- runbook entries for operational handoff and SRE thresholds

This is a working analysis (draft) intended for planning with Finance and Platform teams. Numbers are scenario outputs, not orders.

Assumptions used across scenarios (shared):
- Hosted API demand growth baseline: +18% q/q for token throughput in 2026 unless model upgrades increase per-token cost.
- Average per-request sequence length stable at 120 tokens; peak conversational flows can hit 512 tokens on sampling tests.
- Preferred GPU classes: H100 for high-throughput dedicated shards (latency-sensitive), A100-80GB for mixed workloads, A800 reserved for cost-sensitive embedding-heavy workloads in APAC pilot.
- Target utilization goals: 65–85% active utilization on long-lived reserved pools; 30–45% for burst/spot pools.
- Typical lead time for committed provisioning (cloud reservations + onboarding): 6–10 weeks; additional 2–3 weeks for networking/KMS onboarding in Private deployments.

Scenario A — Conservative (pay-as-you-go heavy; low capital commitments) [Low risk]
Summary: Slow reserve growth, rely on spot and short-term bursts. Good for unpredictable model churn.
Target inventory by 2026-12:
- NA: H100: 160 units; A100-80GB: 200 units; Spot/Burst capacity ~120 units (mixed)
- EU: H100: 80 units; A100-80GB: 120 units; Spot/Burst ~60 units
- APAC: A800: 100 units; A100-80GB: 40 units; Spot/Burst ~80 units
Utilization profile (end of 2026):
- NA reserved pools: 62% average; spot pools: 38% average (higher volatility)
- EU reserved pools: 58% average; spot pools: 35%
- APAC reserved pools: 48% average (still ramping); spot pools: 40%
Operational impacts and triggers:
- Trigger to convert spot->reserved: 6 consecutive weeks where spot preemptions cause >5% error-rate or 15% latency tail increase on SLOs.
- Finance limit: no region exceeds a monthly reserved commitment increase >15% without exec review.

Scenario B — Balanced (recommended baseline) [Medium risk/benefit]
Summary: Mix of reserved capacity for steady traffic and burst pools to absorb headroom; regional parity emphasis for NA/EU with accelerated APAC pilot.
Target inventory by 2026-12:
- NA: H100: 320 units; A100-80GB: 240 units; spot/burst: 160 units
- EU: H100: 160 units; A100-80GB: 140 units; spot/burst: 80 units
- APAC: H100 (pilot): 48 units; A800: 140 units; spot/burst: 100 units
Utilization profile (end of 2026):
- NA reserved pools: 72% avg; burst pools: 30–40%
- EU reserved pools: 68% avg; burst pools: 32%
- APAC reserved pools: 55% avg (ramp); burst pools: 38%
Phased rollout timeline (Balanced):
- 2026-02: APAC pilot procurement commences for A800 and small H100 cage (48 units).
- 2026-04: NA H100 tranche #1 (160 units) activated; routing policy: 85% traffic to NA for hosted API with multi-region failover.
- 2026-06: EU H100 tranche #1 (80 units) activated and paired with NA for redundancy; begin cross-region read-only KV cache replication.
- 2026-09: NA H100 tranche #2 (160 units) activated; automated rollout via Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% within 72 hours if no regressions.
- 2026-11: APAC scale to full pilot capacity (A800 140 + H100 48) and enable burst routing for region-local traffic.
Operational triggers and telemetry (Balanced):
- Provision additional reserved capacity when regional 7-day weighted utilization >78% AND 14-day growth >12%.
- Scale back (not decommit) burst capacity when 30-day utilization <20% and cost delta >10% vs baseline.
- Add H100 to APAC only if latency-sensitive endpoints see 95th percentile latency >2.3s and volume >5% of global requests.

Scenario C — Aggressive growth (market capture / enterprise SLAs) [Higher risk, lower unit cost]
Summary: Heavy reserved commitments with aggressive regional parity and predictable unit economics for enterprise customers. Suitable when ARR growth and committed revenue justify capex.
Target inventory by 2027-06:
- NA: H100: 720 units; A100-80GB: 360 units; Reserved-only strategy for critical routes
- EU: H100: 360 units; A100-80GB: 200 units
- APAC: H100: 200 units; A800: 200 units; add private-onprem nodes for two key enterprise customers in APAC (20 racks)
Utilization profile (mid-2027):
- Target reserved utilization: 82–86% (tight packing with aggressive packing scheduler)
- Burst/spot: <20% overall (used primarily for training jobs and batch embeddings)
Key operational investments required:
- Capacity planner automation to run weekly placement simulations and recommend swap/reshuffle across AZs to avoid hot AZs.
- Additional SRE headcount for 24x7 regional incident coverage: +2 FTE EU, +3 FTE NA, +1 FTE APAC (on-call overlap)
- Pre-negotiated liability/credits with cloud vendor for replacement windows and capacity guarantees.

Cross-scenario considerations and tactical playbook:
1) Buffer sizing: Always maintain a functional buffer of ~8–12% of reserved capacity per region to absorb software rollouts and failover. Buffer is separate from burst pools.
2) Cold-start ramping: When activating a tranche, enable staged traffic (canary) plus a pre-warming traffic generator that primes KV caches and FPGA/optimizers to avoid token-latency spikes.
3) Quantization policy: Route cost-sensitive embedding jobs to A800 in APAC when model accuracy tests (in eval harness) show <1.5% quality delta vs H100.
4) Network / KMS: Budget 2 extra weeks for cross-account KMS policies and VPC peering in Private deployments; include this in GANTT-based ETA.
5) Cost control: Use committed + convertible reservations for NA and EU; spot-heavy APAC for cost experiments. Evaluate convertible reservations if expected architecture will shift between A100/H100 mix.

Runbook snippets (operational):
- On sustained 5-minute CPU/GPU scheduler queuing >100ms and 95th token latency spike >1.8x baseline -> escalate to on-call infra (pager: #infra-oncall) and mark impacted routes for auto-fallback to secondary pools.
- If spot preemptions >3% of workload in a 24h window -> automatically reassign 20% of critical load to reserved pool and flag finance for capacity conversion review.
- Rolling expansion flow: order -> provisioning -> pre-warm bench -> canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% (each step min 48h unless safety gates clear faster).

Risks and mitigations:
- Vendor availability: Maintain at least two cloud region types per geography (primary and fallback) and a small private/offline footprint to handle vendor outages.
- Model changes: If a new model release increases per-token GPU utilization by >20%, treat as an immediate provisioning trigger for short-term burst capacity and initiate scenario re-evaluation.
- Cost overruns: Implement weekly cost burn dashboard alerts; if weekly burn > forecast by 12% for two consecutive weeks, halt non-critical spot experiments.

Next actions (short-term checklist):
- Week 1 (owner: Aditi): Lock scenario choice for FY26 planning (Balanced recommended) and circulate to Finance/Platform leads. Link: JIRA INFRA-3245.
- Week 2 (owner: Marco): Begin procurement approvals for NA H100 tranche #1 (target 160 units). Create purchase ticket and estimate commit.
- Week 3 (owner: Priya): Draft APAC pilot onboarding checklist for KMS, DNS, routing; schedule networking windows with cloud partner.
- Week 4 (owner: Sam): Implement telemetry triggers (7-day weighted utilization + 14-day growth) in capacity-dashboard and add alerting to PagerDuty.

Questions for leadership:
- Appetite for long-term reserved commitments (3-year convertible) vs 1-year: prefer 3-year for unit cost savings but requires growth conviction.
- Tolerance for spot experimentation in APAC vs strict reserved-only for enterprise accounts.

Appendix: quick reference table (selected numbers)
Region | Scenario B end-2026 reserved H100 | Scenario B end-2026 A100-80GB | burst/spot
NA | 320 | 240 | 160
EU | 160 | 140 | 80
APAC | 48 (H100) + 140 (A800) | 40 (A100) | 100

Notes: This doc is intentionally scenario-driven; please comment inline with region-specific constraints (legal/GDPR for EU private, telecom peering for APAC providers).
